question:
Refer to the exhibit. The network management system that is located at 192.168.10.10 and port 2000 must receive traps from the Cisco UCS Manager called UCSM. The community name is Cisco123! and the SNMP version must be the most secure. These two commands have already been configured on Cisco UCSM:
UCS-A# scope monitoring -
UCS-A/monitoring # enable snmp -
Which command set completes the SNMP configuration?
context: Topology: NMS (192.168.10.10, port 2000) <-- snmpv3 trap -- UCSM (192.168.10.20, port 443).
imageNote: Diagram: NMS (192.168.10.10, port 2000) receives an snmpv3 trap from UCSM (192.168.10.20, port 443).
options:
UCS-A/monitoring* # create snmp-trap 192.168.10.20:443
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set community Cisco123!
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # send events
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set version v2
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # commit-buffer

UCS-A/monitoring* # create snmp-trap 192.168.10.10
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set community Cisco123!
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set port 2000
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set version v3
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # commit-buffer

UCS-A/monitoring* # create snmp-trap 192.168.10.20
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set community Cisco123!
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set port 443
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set version v3
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # commit-buffer

UCS-A/monitoring* # create snmp-trap 192.168.10.10:2000
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set community Cisco123!
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # send events
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # set version v2
UCS-A/monitoring/snmp-trap* # commit-buffer
theory: Configuring an SNMP trap receiver in Cisco UCS Manager CLI uses 'create snmp-trap <destination-IP>' (not IP:port syntax, and not the NMS's own management address confused with UCSM's), followed by setting the community string, the destination UDP port, and the SNMP version. Because SNMPv3 is the most secure version (offering authentication and encryption, unlike v1/v2c), and the NMS listens at 192.168.10.10 on port 2000, the command set must target that specific host/port combination with 'set version v3' — using the wrong destination address, embedding the port in the create command incorrectly, or selecting v2 would fail the security or addressing requirement. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Manager Administration, SNMP Configuration)
